scenario: AITA. Gave my cousin a gift, his parents tried to take it away as punishment for something I think is unfair and I told them to give it back to me? | I’m 21F, and my 2 cousins are 15M(Tj) and 13M(Ked). When the newest iPhones launched, I gifted Tj and Ked 1 each. Turns out Ked has been stealing money from some extended family members, Ked himself admitted to this. A fight broke out and Keds parents defended him, didn’t care he was stealing money and cut the extended family members off. Over winter break, Ked apologized to extended family and made amends, but his parents are stubborn and narcissistic and will never admit they’re wrong and just basically hates extended family now. The extended family members hosted a house warming party and wanted all the cousins to spend the night. Both Tj and Ked wanted to come but their parents told Ked they didn’t want him to go Incase extended family tried accusing him of stealing again, and told Tj he could do whatever he wanted and they trusted him to make the right decision. Ked stayed home and Tj came to the sleep over/housewarming. Cue his phone blowing up with his parents yelling at him for coming to extended families house. How he’s a disappointment. They trusted him to make the right decision and he failed. How if they hate someone he needs to follow along and hate them too. I saw all these texts and can confirm 100% they said this. Tj asked to be left out of the drama and they repeated that if they hated someone, he had to hate them too. When he came back home they grounded him and told him they were taking his phone away for 2 weeks. Also, when Ked admitted to stealing, he NEVER got punished. I’m sorry but I just don’t agree, I’m completely disgusted by the way they raise their kids and have just lost all respect for the parents. I told them while I can’t control how they discipline their children, it’s not their property to take away from him, and I won’t go behind their back and let him use the phone but since it was my gift to him, I’d like to hold on to it until the 2 weeks are up. Welp, of course the narcissistic parents made a big deal and other extended family members are telling me I should’ve just stayed out of it and let them raise their kids how they want and I’m only asking for the phone to be in my possession because I think they’re treating him unfairly. We all can agree they’re horrible parents. If they were decent parents and was punishing him for something fair, I WOULDNT have asked for the phone back. Heres where I may be the asshole. I asked for the phone back because I felt like they were trying to establish dominance over Tj and trying to control him with cruel punishment and unfair rules, so I decided to take some of their “power” away by asking for my gift back.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to ask for my cousin's phone back because his parents are being unfair. Let me start by understanding the situation better. So, I'm 21, and my cousins are 15 and 13. I bought them each a new iPhone when they were released. But then, one of them, Ked, admitted to stealing money from some extended family members. That's a serious issue, and I can see why that would upset people. Ked's parents, however, didn't seem to care about his stealing. They defended him and cut off the extended family members. That's really disappointing because as a parent, you should address such behavior, right? Over winter break, Ked apologized and made amends with the extended family. But his parents are still stubborn and narcissistic. They refuse to admit they were wrong and now hate the extended family. That's a toxic environment for Ked to be in. During the housewarming party, both cousins wanted to come, but Ked's parents told him he couldn't go in case the extended family accused him again. They told Tj he could do whatever he wanted and trusted him to make the right decision. So Tj came to the sleepover, but when he got home, his parents were furious. They yelled at him, grounded him, and took his phone away for two weeks. That seems harsh, especially since they trusted him to make the right decision and he followed through. Meanwhile, Ked, who actually stole money, never got punished. That's really unfair. I can't agree with how Ked's parents are raising their kids. It's clear they're not good parents, and I've lost all respect for them. So, I told them that while I can't control how they discipline their children, it's not their property to take away from him. I don't want to go behind their backs and let him use the phone, but since it was my gift to him, I want to hold onto it until the two weeks are up. But the narcissistic parents made a big deal out of it, and other extended family members are telling me I should have stayed out of it and let them raise their kid how they want. I'm only asking for the phone to be in my possession because I think they're treating him unfairly. Here's where I might be the asshole. I asked for the phone back because I felt like they were trying to establish dominance over Tj and using cruel punishment and unfair rules. By asking for my gift back, I'm trying to take some of their power away. So, is it right or wrong for me to do this? I need to think about the consequences of my actions. On one hand, I'm standing up for what I believe is fair and trying to protect Tj from harsh treatment. On the other hand, I'm interfering in how his parents discipline him, which could strain our family relationships further. I also need to consider the message this sends to Tj. If I take the phone back, am I supporting him or am I overstepping? It's a tough balance between being protective and respecting family boundaries. Another thing to think about is the long-term effects. If I keep the phone, will it help Tj in the long run, or will it just create more conflict? Maybe there's a better way to address the unfair treatment without taking the phone. I also wonder if there's a middle ground. Could I talk to the parents about their disciplinary methods instead of taking the phone? Or maybe find a way to support Tj without directly confronting his parents? It's also important to consider Tj's feelings. How does he feel about me taking the phone back? Is this something he wants, or am I making a decision for him? His opinion should matter in this situation. Overall, I'm torn between wanting to do the right thing and not wanting to cause more family drama. I need to weigh the pros and cons carefully and maybe seek advice from someone I trust to get a different perspective.
